Anyways back to the actual plot now!

I had previously made a jammer similar to this before although it was on a perf board and was constructed due to a temporary lapse in judgement from excessive flux fumes.

![tony-start-was-able-to-build-this-in-a-cave](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/4f646461caf624410daba85cdf8f52354ca4774c992f0347ecb6af01fe81ad6c.png)

Although I am not a trillionaire

Features of this project:

1. 0.96" OLED for GUI/
2. 3 control buttons
3. 2 NRF24 modules
4. ESP32 c3 super mini based
5. Debug header/iic pins exposed

I also added some extra caps to stabilize  the voltage rails on the nrf modules.

# Made the PCB

For the layout it was pretty easy, the layout is actually quite similar to my mp3 player that i made in week 4. mostly because both use an oled and a few buttons, I added a few holes to serve as mounting holes for the model in CAD and the board is not portable thus needs a powerbank or a phone to run it. Anyways i spent some time making it look as good as possible and heres the result!

### 2026-11-05: # Got some firmware and made the repo!

**1.5h**

# Got some firmware and made the repo!

So, something that id like to clarify is that I DID NOT WRITE THE FIRMWARE! I Have used the firmware from [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SI2MIFB81pw), definitely recommend that you check this out! Mr. littlehakr is an absolute made man and his projects are extremely cool and innovative.

Heres the repo that he shared on his video

[GitHub Link](https://github.com/dkyazzentwatwa/cypher-jammer-mini)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/07b1a9c43e3f29cdbfd5125c08e1890dab7233e1d3dc6828382c233a5078d98a.png)

This is his jammer which is made on a perfboard, I have ensured that the pin outs match so that the firmware can remain unchanged. Think of my project as a more upgraded and polished version of his project!

Also funfact, I made WANDA once before too, with the same code that the littlehakr shared on a breadboard where it worked remarkably well for a prototype, so to think of it this is her rebirth into a concrete form on a fr4 substrate.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/ac14173c6f8f839f4b7519196024703ef6dc4a7e0858283885c9093c2963c40e.png)

The only image documenting the previous build on a breadboard.
